statement: Let a valid trip be a sequence (p_0,...,p_k) of integers such that each p_i satisfies 0 <= p_i < n, the values p_0,...,p_k are pairwise distinct, and for every j with 0 <= j < k there is an entry [u,v,c] in highways with {u,v} = {p_j,p_{j+1}}; because no unordered endpoint pair repeats, this entry and its toll c are unique. Its cost is the sum of these k unique tolls. The function returns a result r, and: if at least one valid trip exists, r equals the maximum cost of a valid trip; if no valid trip exists, r = -1.
preconditions: n, k, and every entry of highways are 64-bit integers; 2 <= n <= 15; 1 <= len(highways) <= 50; each highways[i] has length 3; for each i, writing highways[i] = [u,v,c], we have 0 <= u < n, 0 <= v < n, u != v, and 0 <= c <= 100; no two entries have the same unordered pair of endpoints; 1 <= k <= 50.

statement: For every input satisfying the preconditions, the function returns a result r (it does not fail, panic, or overflow).
preconditions: n, k, and every entry of highways are 64-bit integers; 2 <= n <= 15; 1 <= len(highways) <= 50; each highways[i] has length 3; for each i, writing highways[i] = [u,v,c], we have 0 <= u < n, 0 <= v < n, u != v, and 0 <= c <= 100; no two entries have the same unordered pair of endpoints; 1 <= k <= 50.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r with r != -1, there exists a valid trip whose cost is r, where a valid trip is a sequence (p_0,...,p_k) of pairwise distinct integers in [0,n-1] such that each consecutive pair is connected by a highway, and its cost is the sum of the k unique corresponding highway tolls.
preconditions: n, k, and every entry of highways are 64-bit integers; 2 <= n <= 15; 1 <= len(highways) <= 50; each highways[i] has length 3; for each i, writing highways[i] = [u,v,c], we have 0 <= u < n, 0 <= v < n, u != v, and 0 <= c <= 100; no two entries have the same unordered pair of endpoints; 1 <= k <= 50.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r with r != -1, every valid trip has cost at most r, where a valid trip is a sequence (p_0,...,p_k) of pairwise distinct integers in [0,n-1] such that each consecutive pair is connected by a highway, and its cost is the sum of the k unique corresponding highway tolls.
preconditions: n, k, and every entry of highways are 64-bit integers; 2 <= n <= 15; 1 <= len(highways) <= 50; each highways[i] has length 3; for each i, writing highways[i] = [u,v,c], we have 0 <= u < n, 0 <= v < n, u != v, and 0 <= c <= 100; no two entries have the same unordered pair of endpoints; 1 <= k <= 50.

statement: Whenever the function returns r = -1, there is no valid trip, where a valid trip is a sequence (p_0,...,p_k) of pairwise distinct integers in [0,n-1] such that each consecutive pair is connected by a highway.
preconditions: n, k, and every entry of highways are 64-bit integers; 2 <= n <= 15; 1 <= len(highways) <= 50; each highways[i] has length 3; for each i, writing highways[i] = [u,v,c], we have 0 <= u < n, 0 <= v < n, u != v, and 0 <= c <= 100; no two entries have the same unordered pair of endpoints; 1 <= k <= 50.

statement: If there exists a valid trip, where a valid trip is a sequence (p_0,...,p_k) of pairwise distinct integers in [0,n-1] such that each consecutive pair is connected by a highway, then the function returns a result r with r != -1.
preconditions: n, k, and every entry of highways are 64-bit integers; 2 <= n <= 15; 1 <= len(highways) <= 50; each highways[i] has length 3; for each i, writing highways[i] = [u,v,c], we have 0 <= u < n, 0 <= v < n, u != v, and 0 <= c <= 100; no two entries have the same unordered pair of endpoints; 1 <= k <= 50.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r with r != -1, 0 <= r <= k * M, where M is the maximum toll among all entries of highways.
preconditions: n, k, and every entry of highways are 64-bit integers; 2 <= n <= 15; 1 <= len(highways) <= 50; each highways[i] has length 3; for each i, writing highways[i] = [u,v,c], we have 0 <= u < n, 0 <= v < n, u != v, and 0 <= c <= 100; no two entries have the same unordered pair of endpoints; 1 <= k <= 50.

statement: If k >= n, the function returns -1.
preconditions: n, k, and every entry of highways are 64-bit integers; 2 <= n <= 15; 1 <= len(highways) <= 50; each highways[i] has length 3; for each i, writing highways[i] = [u,v,c], we have 0 <= u < n, 0 <= v < n, u != v, and 0 <= c <= 100; no two entries have the same unordered pair of endpoints; 1 <= k <= 50.

statement: If k > len(highways), the function returns -1.
preconditions: n, k, and every entry of highways are 64-bit integers; 2 <= n <= 15; 1 <= len(highways) <= 50; each highways[i] has length 3; for each i, writing highways[i] = [u,v,c], we have 0 <= u < n, 0 <= v < n, u != v, and 0 <= c <= 100; no two entries have the same unordered pair of endpoints; 1 <= k <= 50.

statement: If k = 1, the function returns r, where r is the maximum toll among all entries of highways.
preconditions: n, k, and every entry of highways are 64-bit integers; 2 <= n <= 15; 1 <= len(highways) <= 50; each highways[i] has length 3; for each i, writing highways[i] = [u,v,c], we have 0 <= u < n, 0 <= v < n, u != v, and 0 <= c <= 100; no two entries have the same unordered pair of endpoints; 1 <= k <= 50; k = 1.

statement: If every entry [u,v,c] in highways has c = 0, then the function returns r, and r = 0 if there exists a valid trip (a sequence (p_0,...,p_k) of pairwise distinct integers in [0,n-1] such that each consecutive pair is connected by a highway), otherwise r = -1.
preconditions: n, k, and every entry of highways are 64-bit integers; 2 <= n <= 15; 1 <= len(highways) <= 50; each highways[i] has length 3; for each i, writing highways[i] = [u,v,c], we have 0 <= u < n, 0 <= v < n, u != v, and 0 <= c <= 100; no two entries have the same unordered pair of endpoints; 1 <= k <= 50; every entry [u,v,c] in highways has c = 0.

statement: For every list hs' that is a permutation of highways, if maximum_cost(n, highways, k) returns r and maximum_cost(n, hs', k) returns r', then r = r'.
preconditions: n, k, and every entry of highways are 64-bit integers; 2 <= n <= 15; 1 <= len(highways) <= 50; each highways[i] has length 3; for each i, writing highways[i] = [u,v,c], we have 0 <= u < n, 0 <= v < n, u != v, and 0 <= c <= 100; no two entries have the same unordered pair of endpoints; 1 <= k <= 50; hs' is any permutation of the list highways.

statement: For every list hs' obtained from highways by reversing any subset of the highway endpoint pairs, if maximum_cost(n, highways, k) returns r and maximum_cost(n, hs', k) returns r', then r = r'.
preconditions: n, k, and every entry of highways are 64-bit integers; 2 <= n <= 15; 1 <= len(highways) <= 50; each highways[i] has length 3; for each i, writing highways[i] = [u,v,c], we have 0 <= u < n, 0 <= v < n, u != v, and 0 <= c <= 100; no two entries have the same unordered pair of endpoints; 1 <= k <= 50; hs' is any list obtained from highways by replacing each entry [u,v,c] with either [u,v,c] or [v,u,c].

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r with r != -1, r >= k * m, where m is the minimum toll among all entries of highways.
preconditions: n, k, and every entry of highways are 64-bit integers; 2 <= n <= 15; 1 <= len(highways) <= 50; each highways[i] has length 3; for each i, writing highways[i] = [u,v,c], we have 0 <= u < n, 0 <= v < n, u != v, and 0 <= c <= 100; no two entries have the same unordered pair of endpoints; 1 <= k <= 50.

statement: If k = 2, the function returns a result r, and r = -1 if there are no two distinct entries [u,v,c] and [u',v',c'] in highways with the sets {u,v} and {u',v'} intersecting in exactly one city; otherwise r is the maximum, over all such pairs of entries, of c + c'.
preconditions: n, k, and every entry of highways are 64-bit integers; 2 <= n <= 15; 1 <= len(highways) <= 50; each highways[i] has length 3; for each i, writing highways[i] = [u,v,c], we have 0 <= u < n, 0 <= v < n, u != v, and 0 <= c <= 100; no two entries have the same unordered pair of endpoints; 1 <= k <= 50; k = 2.
